Our Origins & Purpose

Cooking with the Ancient Energy of Fire & Soil

Verdant Hearth began in 2012 with a radical commitment: banish electrical heat and fossil gas from our kitchen entirely, surrendering every pan and skewer to sustainably harvested Oregon alder, white oak, and fruitwood.

Surrounding our live hearth is an edible botanical greenhouse where we harvest mountain thyme, flowering nasturtiums, and lemon verbena minutes before they grace your table. We celebrate 42 small-family regenerative farms who revive heirloom seeds, building a culinary landscape as vibrant and enduring as our forests.

Spring Harvest Wild Morels, Verdant Ramps & Pacific Wood-Fired Offerings

As Pacific Northwest soils awaken from winter dormancy, our partner farms across the Willamette and Hood River valleys yield fleeting treasures: forest morels, tender ramps, sweet English peas, and delicate stinging nettles. Every plate reflects the brief, luminous window between the last frost and early summer sun.

Rooted In Regenerative Soil:
🌾 Rainshadow Heritage Farms 🌾 Cascadia Wild Foraging Co. 🌾 Willamette Stone Creamery 🌾 Coastal Tides Day-Boat
Peak Spring Harvest Ingredients: Gathered at sunrise across the Cascade foothills

Four guiding principles shape every flame we kindle, every seed we source, and every bottle we unseal.

01
✦

Wood-Fired Hearth Craft

Every hot dish touches real seasoned Oregon oak, fruitwood, and alder embers for an irreplaceable depth of smokiness.

02
✦

42 Regenerative Partners

We partner directly with small biodynamic growers who prioritize soil health, heritage seed banks, and chemical-free stewardship.

Living Botanical Cellar

04

Closed-Loop Circular Ecology

98% of kitchen scraps are composted and returned directly to our partner farm beds within forty-eight hours.

Artisans of Flame & Earth

Meet the Culinary Masters

Led by passion for wood-fired gastronomy and seasonal botanicals, our culinary team transforms raw terroir into unforgettable dining memories.

Live-Fire Hearth Master
Executive Chef & Co-Founder

Julian Thorne

Raised along the Oregon coastline, Julian honed his culinary mastery in Basque country hearths and French countryside kitchens before returning home to establish Verdant Hearth in 2012. He believes wood-ember cooking is an instinctual dance between wind, wood moisture, and radiant heat.

Distinction ★ James Beard Foundation Nominee
Meet Artisan & View Dishes →
Botanical Confections
Head Pastry Chef

Elena Rostova

Elena treats pastry as an extension of botanical medicine and agricultural heritage. Rather than relying on refined sugars and bleached flours, she crafts desserts using whole grains stone-milled in house, wildflower mountain honeys, and foraged forest berries.

Distinction ★ Valrhona Pastry Innovator
Meet Artisan & View Dishes →
Biodynamic Terroir
Master Sommelier & Beverage Director

Matthieu Laurent

Born in Burgundy into a family of vignerons, Matthieu spent two decades exploring natural vineyards throughout France, Italy, and Oregon before anchoring our beverage cellar.

Distinction ★ Court of Master Sommeliers (DipWSET)
Meet Artisan & View Dishes →
Precision Fire Line Directing
Chef de Cuisine

Marcus Rivera

Marcus oversees evening line operations, coordinating timing between the hearth grill, stone bake oven, and vegetable ember pits so every plate arrives at peak thermodynamic beauty.

Distinction ★ Charcuterie Guild Medalist

Ethnobotany
Lead Forager & Botanical Specialist

Clara Sterling

With a Master of Science in Ethnobotany, Clara forages through private forest tracts in the Pacific Northwest, sustainably gathering wild mushrooms, elderflowers, nettles, and edible blossoms.

Distinction ★ Pacific Northwest Wild Flora Scholar

In-House Stone Milling
Head Artisan Baker & Miller

Thomas Lind

Common Inquiries

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about dining policies, private events, dietary accommodations, and reservations.

How far in advance can I book a table at Verdant Hearth?

Reservations open 30 days in advance at 9:00 AM on the first day of each month for standard dining and the Chef’s Counter. We also reserve a portion of the bar and garden terrace nightly for walk-in guests on a first-come, first-served basis.

Can you accommodate dietary restrictions (vegan, gluten-free, nut allergies)?

Over 65% of our menu is naturally gluten-free or can be adapted without losing depth of flavor. We take allergies seriously—please note any dietary requirements when booking so our kitchen can prepare customized broths and garnishes.

Is there a dress code for evening dinner service?

We embrace an upscale casual atmosphere. Smart casual attire is welcomed—neat denim, collared shirts, dresses, or tailored jackets are typical. We ask that guests avoid athletic sportswear and beachwear.

What is your corkage fee policy?

You are welcome to bring special bottles from your personal cellar not represented on our current wine list. Our corkage fee is $35 per 750ml bottle (maximum 2 bottles per party). We happily waive one fee for each bottle purchased from our list.

Do you offer valet parking or nearby garage access?

Complimentary valet parking is available at our main entrance on Botanical Way starting at 4:30 PM Wednesday through Sunday. Additional covered parking is available two doors down at Hearth Quarter Garage with 2 hours validated.

Can I book a private event or buy out the restaurant?

Yes! Our Botanical Conservatory accommodates private seated dinners for up to 45 guests, and complete restaurant buyouts can host up to 130 guests. Contact our events team via our reservation form or email concierge@verdanthearth.com.

What is your cancellation policy?

We request at least 24 hours notice for standard table cancellations. Chef’s Counter and tasting menus require 48 hours notice to avoid a $45 per guest cancellation fee.

Are children welcome in the restaurant?

Well-behaved young guests are welcome in our main dining room and garden patio. We offer wholesome, fresh hearth flatbreads, roasted chicken, and handmade pasta options that young palates adore.

What woods do you use in your culinary hearth?

We exclusively burn seasoned, sustainably harvested Oregon hardwoods including white oak, red alder, and pruned apple orchard woods. We never burn resinous softwoods like pine or fir in cooking chambers.

Do you offer gift certificates?

Yes! Digital and handcrafted letterpress gift cards are available for purchase online or at the concierge desk, valid for all dining experiences, Chef’s counter tastings, and private events.

What is the Chef’s Counter experience?

The Chef’s Counter is an elevated 8-seat bar directly overlooking our live hearth. Guests enjoy an interactive 7-course tasting menu prepared and introduced directly by Executive Chef Julian Thorne and our sous chefs.

Can I request outdoor dining in the garden or patio?

Our garden patio and covered conservatory are open year-round with radiant heated floors and botanical overhead pergolas. You can select "Conservatory Seating" during your online reservation process.

Have an inquiry not answered above? Email our hospitality concierge at concierge@verdanthearth.com
